segments.arabic:
١١٨٦٠- هند بنت عتبة
بن ربيعة «٢» بن عبد شمس بن عبد مناف القرشيّة «٣»، والدة معاوية بن أبي سفيان.
أخبارها قبل الإسلام مشهورة. وشهدت أحدا، وفعلت ما فعلت بحمزة، ثم كانت تؤلّب على المسلمين إلى أن جاء اللَّه بالفتح فأسلم زوجها ثم أسلمت هي يوم الفتح، وقصّتهما- في قولها عند بيعة النساء: وأن لا يسرقن ولا يزنين، فقالت: وهل تزني الحرّة؟
وعند قوله: وَلا يَقْتُلْنَ أَوْلادَهُنَّ: وقد ربيناهم صغارا وقتلتهم كبارا مشهورة.
ومن طرقه ما أخرجه ابن سعد بسند صحيح مرسل عن الشّعبي، وعن ميمون بن مهران، ففي رواية الشّعبي: وَلا يَزْنِينَ- قالت هند: وهل تزني الحرّة؟ وَلَا تَقْتُلْنَ أَوْلَادَكُنَّ- قالت: أنت قتلتهم.
وفي رواية نحوه، لكن قالت: وهل تركت لنا ولدا يوم بدر، وسؤالها عن أخذها من مال زوجها بغير إذنه ما يكفيها، وهل عليها فيه من حرج- مخرج
في الصّحيحين، وفيه:
«خذي من ماله بالمعروف ما يكفيك وولدك» . وهو من رواية هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، عن عائشة.
(١) أسد الغابة ت (٧٣٤٩)، الاستيعاب ت (٣٥٦٧)، الثقات ٣/ ٤٤٠، أعلام النساء ٥/ ٢٠٣، تجريد أسماء الصحابة ٢/ ٣١٠، الكاشف ٣/ ٤٩٢.
(٢) أسد الغابة ت (٧٣٥٠)، الثقات ٣/ ٤٣٩- أعلام النساء ٥/ ٢٣٩- تجريد أسماء الصحابة ٢/ ٣١٠- أعلام النساء ٥/ ٢٣٩- تجريد أسماء الصحابة ٢/ ٣١٠- أزمنة التاريخ الإسلامي ١٠٠٨- تلقيح فهوم أهل الأثر ٣١٩- وله در السحابة ٨٢٤- الاستيعاب ت (٣٥٦٨) .
(٣) في أ: القرشية العبشمية.
segments.english:
11860—Hind bint Utba

ibn Rabi'a² ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf, the Qurashi woman,³ mother of Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan.

The accounts concerning her before Islam are well known. She was present at Uhud and did what she did to Hamza. She then continued inciting people against the Muslims until Allah brought about the Conquest. Her husband embraced Islam, and she subsequently embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest. Their story is well known, including what she said during the women’s pledge when they were charged “not to steal and not to commit fornication.” She said, “Does a free woman commit fornication?”

And at His words, “and they shall not kill their children,” she said, “We raised them when they were small, and you killed them when they were grown.”

Among the routes by which this is transmitted is what Ibn Sa'd related with a sound but mursal chain from al-Sha'bi, and from Maymun ibn Mihran. In al-Sha'bi’s narration, at “and they shall not commit fornication,” Hind said, “Does a free woman commit fornication?” At “and do not kill your children,” she said, “You killed them.”

The other narration is similar, except that she said, “Did you leave us any child on the day of Badr?”

The report of her asking whether she could take from her husband’s property, without his permission, enough to suffice her, and whether she would incur any blame for doing so, is recorded in the two Sahih collections. It contains:

“Take from his property, according to what is customary, enough to suffice you and your child.”

It is transmitted by Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha.

(1) Usd al-Ghaba, entry 7349; al-Isti'ab, entry 3567; al-Thiqat 3/440; A'lam al-Nisa' 5/203; al-Tajrid 2/310; al-Kashif 3/492.

(2) Usd al-Ghaba, entry 7350; al-Thiqat 3/439; A'lam al-Nisa' 5/239; al-Tajrid 2/310; A'lam al-Nisa' 5/239; al-Tajrid 2/310; Azminat al-Tarikh al-Islami, 1008; Talqih Fuhum Ahl al-Athar, 319; Durr al-Sahaba, 824; al-Isti'ab, entry 3568.

(3) In manuscript A: “the Qurashi al-Abshamiyya woman.”

segments.arabic:
وشذّ عبد اللَّه بن محمّد بن عروة، فقال: عن هشام، عن أبيه، عن هند، أخرجه ابن مندة، وأوله: قالت هند: إني أريد أن أبايع محمدا، قال: قد رأيتك تكفرين. قالت: أي واللَّه، واللَّه ما رأيت اللَّه تعالى عبد حقّ عبادته في هذا المسجد قبل الليلة، واللَّه إن باتوا إلا مصلّين قياما وركوعا وسجودا. قال: فإنك قد فعلت ما فعلت، فاذهبي برجل من قومك معك، فذهبت إلى عمر، فذهب معها فاستأذن لها، فدخلت وهي متنقبة، فذكر قصّة البيعة، وفيه ما قدمته، وفيه: فقالت: إن أبا سفيان رجل بخيل، ولا يعطيني، ما يكفيني إلا ما أخذت منه من غير علمه.. الحديث.
وفيه، عن مرسل الشّعبي المذكور: قالت هند: قد كنت أفنيت من مال أبي سفيان.
فقال أبو سفيان: ما أخذت من مالي فهو حلال.
وقال ابن سعد: قال الواقديّ: لما أسلمت هند جعلت تضرب صنما لها في بيتها بالقدوم حتى فلذته فلذة فلذة، وتقول: كنّا معك في غرور.
قال أبو عمر: ماتت في خلافة عمر بعد أبي بكر بقليل في اليوم الّذي مات فيه أبو قحافة، كذا قال.
وقد ذكر صاحب «الأمثال» ما يدلّ على أنها بقيت إلى خلافة عثمان، بل بعد ذلك، لأنّ أبا سفيان مات في خلافة عثمان بلا خلاف، وقال هذا: قال رجل لمعاوية زوجني هندا، قال: إنها قعدت عن الولد، ولا حاجة إلى الزّواج. قال: فولّني ناحية كذا، فأنشد معاوية:
طلب الأبيض العقوق فلمّا ... أعجزته أراد بيض الأنوق
[الخفيف] يعني أنه طلب ما لا يصل إليه، فلما عجز عنه طلب أبعد منه. ثم رأيت في طبقات ابن سعد الجزم بأنها ماتت في خلافة عثمان.
segments.english:
Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Urwa gave an anomalous version, saying, “From Hisham, from his father, from Hind.” Ibn Manda transmitted it. It begins: Hind said, “I wish to pledge allegiance to Muhammad.” He said, “I have seen you disbelieving.” She said, “Yes, by Allah! By Allah, before tonight I had never seen Allah Most High worshipped in this mosque as He truly ought to be worshipped. By Allah, they spent the night doing nothing but praying—standing, bowing, and prostrating.” He said, “You have done what you have done. Go and take a man from your people with you.” She went to Umar, who went with her and sought permission for her to enter. She entered veiled. The report then recounts the story of the pledge, including what I cited above. It also contains: She said, “Abu Sufyan is a miserly man and does not give me enough; I obtain what suffices me only by taking from him without his knowledge…” to the end of the hadith.

The aforementioned mursal report of al-Sha'bi also contains: Hind said, “I had already used up some of Abu Sufyan's property.”

Abu Sufyan said, “Whatever you have taken from my property is lawful for you.”

Ibn Sa'd said: Al-Waqidi said, “When Hind embraced Islam, she began striking an idol she kept in her house with an adze until she broke it apart, fragment by fragment, saying, ‘We were deluded while we were with you.’”

Abu Umar said: She died during the caliphate of Umar, shortly after Abu Bakr's death, on the same day that Abu Quhafa died. Thus he stated.

The author of al-Amthal mentioned evidence indicating that she remained alive until the caliphate of Uthman—indeed, even beyond it—because Abu Sufyan died during Uthman's caliphate, without dispute. He gave this account: A man said to Muawiya, “Give me Hind in marriage.” Muawiya replied, “She has ceased bearing children, and there is no need for marriage.” The man said, “Then appoint me over such-and-such a district.” Muawiya recited:

He sought the “pregnant white male”; when it proved beyond him,
he desired the eggs of the anuq.

[al-Khafif]

He meant that the man sought something he could not attain and, when unable to obtain it, sought something even more remote. I then found in Ibn Sa'd's al-Tabaqat the categorical statement that she died during the caliphate of Uthman.
